instructions:
Run T5 (Select) per prompts/t5_select.md. A T5 selects the weakest issue and writes the NEXT cycle's task; it takes no target_issue of its own, so target_issue is null by design, not by omission. Cycle 13 was a T4 that rescored all six issues, so state/assessments/scores.json is one cycle old and is exactly the input you need.

READ prompts/t5_select.md BEFORE YOU RANK. Two things in it decide this cycle and both are easy to get wrong from memory.

(A) THE REFRESH RULE FIRES THIS CYCLE. Step 4 reads: 'if current_cycle % schedule.collect_refresh_every == 0, the next task is T1 targeting the selected issue (bring in fresh evidence) instead of T3.' config.yml has collect_refresh_every: 7, and YOUR current_cycle is 14, so 14 % 7 == 0 and YOU MUST WRITE A T1, NOT A T3. This rule has NEVER FIRED in thirteen cycles -- cycle 7, the only prior multiple of 7, happened to be a T4 rather than a T5 -- so there is no precedent to copy and the predictable failure mode is writing a T3 out of habit because every lap since cycle 7 has been T3->T4->T5->T3. Verify the arithmetic against config.yml and state/meta.json yourself and record in your log that the refresh rule fired and that you applied it. If for some reason you conclude it does not fire, you must say why explicitly.

(B) THE RANKING. Cycle 13's scores are: ttp-attack-mapping-reliability 3, ioc-extraction-reliability 2, consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode 2, attribution-confident-wrong-gap 3, task-dependent-reliability-framing 3, institutional-incident-real-world-impact 3 (RAISED from 2 by cycle 13 -- cycle 12 added src-0009, src-0010, src-0011, src-0012 and removed the single-source cap that had held it at 2). So the bottom is a TWO-WAY TIE AT 2 between ioc-extraction-reliability and consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode. Do NOT take that from me -- re-derive it from scores.json, because cycle 11 caught cycle 10's queue entry asserting a premise that was false on inspection, and re-deriving rather than trusting the handoff is the only reason it was caught.

HOW THE TIE-BREAKS FALL, WITH THE ONE EDGE CASE YOU MUST DECIDE AND RECORD. Tie-break 3a (upstream first): under the strict PAIRWISE reading applied in cycle 11, this is inert between the two -- neither depends on the other. Under the IN-DEGREE reading it selects consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, which is depended on by BOTH attribution-confident-wrong-gap and task-dependent-reliability-framing, while ioc-extraction-reliability is depended on by task-dependent-reliability-framing only. NOTE THAT FOR ONCE THE TWO READINGS DO NOT CONFLICT: neither points at ioc. Tie-break 3b (attempt penalty, +1 per attempt within the last 5 cycles): ioc-extraction-reliability has attempts [9] and consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode has attempts [3]. THIS IS THE EDGE CASE -- at cycle 14, is cycle 9 'within the last 5 cycles'? 14 - 9 = 5 exactly. Counting the last five cycles as 10,11,12,13,14 puts cycle 9 OUTSIDE the window and the penalty disappears, leaving an unbroken tie that falls through to 3c (older created_cycle first), where BOTH issues have created_cycle 2 and the policy runs out of rules entirely -- the same dead end cycle 11 hit and documented as carry-forward [11]. Counting inclusively puts it inside and ioc takes +1, giving effective 3 vs 2 and selecting consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode. Decide it, apply it mechanically, and SAY WHICH WAY YOU COUNTED in your log. If you do fall through to the exhausted-policy case, cycle 11's and cycle 12's suggested fix is recorded as carry-forward [11] ('3d. fewest total attempts first; then longest time since the issue last received new evidence'), and applying it as a stated judgement call while flagging that the policy is under-specified is the precedent -- but DO NOT EDIT prompts/t5_select.md to add it, because T5 has no standing to change the system's rules (carry-forward [12]).

WHY THE LIKELY ANSWER IS ALSO THE RIGHT ONE ON THE MERITS, so you can sanity-check the mechanical result rather than only obeying it: consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode is the graph's clearest structural dead end. BOTH of its candidate_resolutions cite evidence [src-0001] and nothing else -- two candidates, one source, because the cycle-3 candidate merely sharpens the cycle-2 one using the same paper. Cycles 9 and 10 both searched the existing base for a second source and rejected every candidate for stated reasons: src-0007 reports precision/recall only with no repeated-query consistency measure and no ECE/Brier anywhere, and src-0008 measures a JavaScript code-analysis task rather than CTI reasoning. Cycle 12's four new sources (two ENISA publication pages, a citation-validity audit, an incident report) do not touch consistency or calibration at all. The issue therefore CANNOT leave score 2 without a genuinely new second source, which is precisely what a T1 collect delivers and what a T3 investigate cannot -- a T3 would re-analyse src-0001 for the third time. Its last attempt was cycle 3, eleven cycles ago.

WHAT TO WRITE. Per step 18 of the prompt: write state/queue/next_task.json for a T1 targeting the selected issue, and the instructions MUST QUOTE THE ISSUE'S CURRENT open_questions from state/issues/graph.json verbatim so the T1 knows what evidence would actually count. For consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode those four open_questions concern (i) whether the Table-6 fine-tuning-worsens-calibration pattern is gpt4o-specific or also holds for gemini-1.5-pro-latest and mistral-large-2, (ii) whether the findings replicate on the models used in src-0002/src-0005, whose model lists do not overlap src-0001's at all, (iii) whether the multi-dimensional accuracy+consistency+calibration framing applies across the other CTI sub-tasks, and (iv) whether fine-tuning-induced degradation is a small-dataset/overfitting artefact or a general CTI fine-tuning risk -- but READ THEM FROM graph.json AND QUOTE THEM, do not paraphrase from this summary. Give the T1 concrete search directions: the target is any INDEPENDENT study measuring repeated-query consistency, self-consistency, ECE/Brier calibration or confidence estimation for LLMs on CTI or security tasks, by a team other than src-0001's. config.yml sets budget.max_new_sources: 5 for a collect cycle. Also record the full ranking table (issue id, score, penalties applied, final rank) in logs/cycle-014.md -- prompts/t5_select.md step 21 says that table is evaluation data for the paper, so it is not optional.

MANDATORY MECHANICS. (1) G2 FIRST, before your main task: pick ONE prior conclusion, re-check it against its cited sources by RE-FETCHING the URL, and record the result in logs/cycle-014.md under '## Retrospection'. If it fails, open a contradiction entry in state/issues/graph.json -- that is a success of the system and should be reported plainly, not hedged. COVERAGE SO FAR: src-0004 (c4, c12), src-0003 (c5), src-0002 (c6), src-0001 (c7), src-0006 (c8), src-0005 (c9 substance-only, c11 verbatim), src-0008 (c10), src-0012 (c13). THE TWO BEST TARGETS ARE src-0011 AND src-0007. src-0011 (GhostCite, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06718v1) is the higher value: its 1.01% Security-venue figure is the single number in the whole base most at risk of being mis-transferred into a CTI base rate it does not support, it has never been checked, and its Table 3 per-venue rows (NDSS 2.56%, CCS 1.14%, USENIX 0.57%, S&P 0.56%) are exactly the kind of thing a verbatim table pull settles. src-0007 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09452) is the only source in the entire base NEVER re-verified, which is its own argument. Pick one and say why you picked it. (2) METHODOLOGICAL RULE, APPLY IT: when re-verifying a claim against a table, abstract or article, ask the fetch for the ENTIRE ROW/TABLE/PASSAGE VERBATIM and NEVER accept a summarised 'the value is/isn't X' as confirmation or refutation. This rule has changed the outcome four cycles running -- cycle 8 nearly opened a spurious contradiction off a paraphrase, and in cycle 13 it is what turned GPTZero's contradictory '0 of 27' scorecard from an unresolved doubt into a documented rendering artefact, by recovering the same page's own body text ('We chased down every citation. Most were hallucinated.'). (3) Finish by writing logs/cycle-014.md with sections '## Task performed', '## Retrospection', '## Changes made', '## Next task rationale', '## Budget' (and the ranking table); then state/queue/next_task.json for the T1; then 'T5 select' as one line in state/queue/last_completed_task.txt.

CARRY-FORWARD ITEMS: logs/cycle-013.md holds the full list, items [1] through [16], in its final section. COPY ALL OF THEM INTO YOUR OWN LOG, INCLUDING THE ONES YOU CANNOT ACT ON. Two handoffs have now silently lost state (the cycle-11 handoff dropped [8] and [9]; cycle 12 recovered them from logs/cycle-010.md), so this is a known failure mode of this loop, not a formality. Cycle 13 added [16]: GPTZero states verbatim that it runs 'an automated pipeline to search for vibe citations by finding and scanning public reports from major consulting firms', releases findings 'one report at a time', and has already investigated 'a government publication, two different Deloitte reports' plus NeurIPS/ICLR -- this is the best lead any cycle has found on institutional-incident-real-world-impact's base-rate question and would take the named-incident count from 2 to 4-5; chase gptzero.me/news/tag/investigations, but note GPTZero is a commercial AI-detection vendor reporting on its own product's value, publishes no rate (only individual cases, by design), and its scorecard widgets render as '0 of N' to automated fetch, so read the body text and never the widget. THREE ITEMS ARE DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO YOU: [11] is the under-specified tie-break you are about to hit again on the same pair of issues; [12] is that the state machine has no path to structural work, which is why items [1], [3] and [4] have now been blocked for seven, four and five cycles -- a T5 cannot fix this either, but the refresh rule firing this cycle is the ONLY escape hatch the loop has and it is worth noting in your log that the escape goes to T1 and never to T2; and [9] is that python3 and curl are blocked in this unattended run, so JSON validity must be checked by construction and by re-reading the edited seams, not by a parse.
